title: Ram Charan's Peddi Has Crossed ₹150 Crore Worldwide in Two Days. Telugu Cinema Just Flexed on Everyone.
excerpt: The sports drama is sprinting past every box office milestone despite a controversy that forced the director to publicly apologize and promise to cut scenes.
body:
There is a particular kind of opening that announces itself not with marketing but with mathematics. **Ram Charan's** *Peddi* delivered exactly that — ₹150.49 crore worldwide in 48 hours, an opening so violent it made his own *Game Changer* look like a warm-up lap.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=sF2dj7ycZvA</youtube>

Directed by **Buchi Babu Sana** and produced by **Mythri Movie Makers** in collaboration with Vriddhi Cinemas, the Telugu sports-action drama hit theatres on June 4 and hasn't stopped running since. Day 1 alone brought in ₹51 crore net in India after preview screenings had already raked in ₹18.50 crore. Day 2 added another ₹26.90 crore net domestically, pushing the India total to ₹96.40 crore — within touching distance of the ₹100 crore mark before the weekend even began.

The overseas numbers tell their own story. ₹36 crore gross internationally in two days, with strong holds across the US, Gulf, and Australia. For NRI audiences who grew up watching Ram Charan's father Chiranjeevi redefine Telugu stardom, watching the son casually cross ₹150 crore worldwide before most films have finished their first Friday feels like a generational handshake.

## The Numbers That Matter

Here's what makes Peddi's opening genuinely remarkable: the Telugu version alone recorded 48.81% occupancy on Day 2 — a Friday, not a weekend — across nearly 4,950 shows. Evening and night shows climbed to 57% and 60% respectively, which means audiences weren't just sampling the film. They were settling in.

In Coastal Andhra, *Peddi* outperformed both *Pushpa 2: The Rule* and *Kalki 2898 AD* on the same day count, grossing ₹10.75 crore. The Telugu states contributed ₹25 crore gross on Day 2 alone, tracking alongside the biggest Telugu releases in history.

The Hindi version is doing modest but respectable business at ₹2.25 crore net on Day 2. This was never going to be a Hindi-first film. Ram Charan's pull is concentrated where it always has been — in the Telugu-speaking belt — and the numbers reflect a star whose home market treats him like royalty.

> "Now you can't stop anyone. Every producer is of the opinion that 'Main kyun aage jaau?'" — Trade analyst Taran Adarsh on June's crowded release calendar

June 2026 has nine major releases across four Fridays with over ₹1,400 crore collectively at stake. *Peddi* opened the month by immediately claiming the biggest slice of that pie. Trade experts had warned about screen-sharing battles and divided audiences. Ram Charan's response was to collect ₹96 crore in India net before anyone else could get comfortable.

## The Controversy That Won't Quit

The box office triumph has unfolded against a backdrop of genuine fury. Since its release, *Peddi* has been engulfed in controversy over the portrayal of **Janhvi Kapoor's** character, Achiyyamma. Audiences flagged scenes they described as hypersexualized — close-up camera angles, a kissing sequence during a power cut that many called assault — and the backlash was swift and unsparing.

Director Buchi Babu Sana issued a public apology on X, writing: *"It was never our intention to objectify or disrespect any female character. We have decided to make changes to the concerned portions."*

But the damage had already deepened. Screenshots of private messages reportedly sent by Janhvi to fan clubs surfaced, dating back to October 2025 — during production. In one, she wrote: *"I told him no boob and waist shots."* In another, she revealed that Ram Charan himself had intervened: *"Ram sir is so sweet, he also yelled at him and said you will not take such angles of her ever again."*

The implication is uncomfortable and unavoidable: the actress flagged the problem on set, her co-star backed her up, and the footage still made it into the final cut. The director is now cutting scenes he was warned about a year ago.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZEzK5yIKjL/

## What Comes Next

Trade projections peg the four-day extended weekend at ₹180-185 crore domestically. The ₹200 crore India net mark looks inevitable. After that, the question is whether *Peddi* has legs to run toward ₹300 crore or settles in the ₹200-250 crore range — still a massive hit by any standard.

For Ram Charan, the weekend will confirm what the opening already suggested: he is the most bankable solo Telugu star working today. For the industry, *Peddi* is a case study in something more complicated — a film that can be a commercial juggernaut and an ethical flashpoint at the same time. The audience showed up. They also spoke up. Both things can be true.

*Peddi is currently playing in theatres worldwide in Telugu, Hindi, Tamil, Kannada, and Malayalam.*
